summary: B1/B2 visitor visa — online form, USD 160 fee, in-person interview at the US Embassy in Kathmandu.
overview: Nepali citizens need a B1/B2 visa to visit the United States for tourism, visiting family, or short business trips. There is no e-visa or visa-on-arrival option — every applicant completes the DS-160 form online, pays the fee, and attends an in-person interview at the US Embassy in Kathmandu (or a US consulate elsewhere while abroad).

steps.title: Complete the DS-160 form
steps.description: Fill out the DS-160 nonimmigrant visa application online at ceac.state.gov. Save the confirmation page with your barcode number — you need it for the next steps.

steps.title: Pay the visa application fee
steps.description: Pay the USD 160 MRV (Machine Readable Visa) fee through the official payment channel linked from the US Embassy Kathmandu website.

steps.title: Schedule your interview
steps.description: Book an interview slot at the US Embassy in Kathmandu using your DS-160 confirmation number and fee receipt.

steps.title: Attend the interview
steps.description: Bring your passport, DS-160 confirmation page, fee receipt, a passport photo, and supporting documents (bank statements, employment letter, travel itinerary). The consular officer decides on the spot in most cases.

requiredDocuments: Valid Nepali passport (with at least one blank visa page)
DS-160 confirmation page
Visa fee (MRV) payment receipt
Passport-sized photograph meeting US visa photo requirements
Bank statements showing sufficient funds for your trip
Employment verification letter or, if self-employed, business registration documents and tax records
Evidence of ties to Nepal supporting intent to return — property ownership documents, family documentation, investment records, proof of enrolment (students), or a detailed travel budget
Invitation letter from a US-based contact, if you have one (optional, but can strengthen your application)
Certified English translation for any supporting document not already in English
processingTime: Interview wait times vary by season — check the current wait time on the embassy site before planning travel dates. Visa issuance after interview is often same-day to a few days if approved.
fee: USD 160 (MRV fee), non-refundable regardless of outcome
maxStay: Determined by the immigration officer at the US port of entry, typically up to 6 months

officialLinks.label: US Embassy Kathmandu — Visas
DS-160 Online Application

nearestEmbassy.note: US Embassy Kathmandu handles all Nepal-based applicants directly — no need to travel to a third country.

faqs.q: Can I apply for an e-visa instead of going to the embassy?
faqs.a: No — the US does not offer an e-visa for Nepali citizens; a B1/B2 visa requires an in-person interview at the US Embassy in Kathmandu.

faqs.q: What's the biggest reason applications get refused?
faqs.a: Failing to convincingly demonstrate strong ties to Nepal (a stable job, family, property, or other reasons you're expected to return) is consistently the most common reason for a 214(b) refusal.

notes: Visa refusal does not refund the USD 160 fee, and there's no set limit on how many times you can reapply, but repeated refusals without a change in circumstances rarely succeed. A police clearance certificate is not a routine requirement for B1/B2 tourist applications — the DS-160 form itself asks about any criminal history, and the consular officer can request supporting documents case-by-case, but there's no standing requirement to bring one to your interview. Property ownership documents are commonly used as one form of "ties to Nepal" evidence, alongside family and financial ties — no single document is mandatory, but the stronger and more varied your evidence, the better.
sourceNotes: US Embassy Kathmandu (np.usembassy.gov) and travel.state.gov DS-160/MRV fee schedule.

summary: Standard Visitor visa — apply online, biometrics at VFS Global in Kathmandu, NPR 26,236 for a short-term (up to 6 months) visa.
overview: Nepali citizens need a Standard Visitor visa for any UK visit — tourism, family visits, or short business trips. There's no e-visa or visa-on-arrival option. You apply online via gov.uk, then attend a biometrics appointment at a VFS Global centre in Kathmandu. Standard processing is around 3 weeks after biometrics; faster paid options exist but aren't guaranteed.

steps.title: Apply online
steps.description: Complete the Standard Visitor visa application on gov.uk, specifying the length of visa you need (short-term up to 6 months, or longer multi-entry options up to 10 years).

steps.title: Pay the visa fee
steps.description: Fees are set in GBP but charged in NPR. Pay through the official application process — do not pay anyone offering to bypass this.

steps.title: Book a biometrics appointment
steps.description: Schedule your appointment at the VFS Global Visa Application Centre in Kathmandu (or via TLScontact, depending on current provider) to submit fingerprints and a photo.

steps.title: Attend your appointment and wait for a decision
steps.description: Standard processing is roughly 3 weeks from your biometrics appointment. Priority (5 working days, +£500) and Super Priority (next working day, +£1,000) services exist but availability isn't guaranteed.

requiredDocuments: Valid Nepali passport with at least one blank page
Passport-sized digital photo meeting UK visa photo rules
Bank statements covering the last 6 months, showing sufficient funds for your trip (state figures in both NPR and the GBP equivalent using the official exchange rate at the time of application)
Employment verification letter (or business registration if self-employed), plus a letter from your employer confirming approved leave if you're employed
Travel itinerary and accommodation details for your UK visit
Evidence of ties to Nepal supporting your intent to return — property documents, family ties, or employment
Details of any previous international travel (old passports with visa/entry stamps), if you have them
TB test results, if required based on where you're applying from
Certified English translation for any document not already in English
processingTime: Around 3 weeks standard, after your biometrics appointment. Priority (5 working days) and Super Priority (next working day) are optional paid upgrades, subject to availability.
fee: NPR 26,236 for a short-term visa (up to 6 months, single or multiple entry), as of the official UK government fee schedule for Nepal. Longer multi-entry visas (2/5/10-year) cost significantly more. Priority service +NPR ~67,000 (£500); Super Priority +NPR ~134,000 (£1,000).
maxStay: Up to 6 months per visit on a standard visitor visa, regardless of the visa's overall validity period

Official UK visa fee checker (select Nepal)

nearestEmbassy.note: Biometrics submitted via VFS Global (or current visa application centre partner) in Kathmandu — check gov.uk for the current provider, as this has changed before.

faqs.q: Can I get a multi-year visa instead of applying every time?
faqs.a: Yes — the UK Standard Visitor visa can be issued for 6 months, or as a longer 2, 5, or 10-year multi-entry visa (at a higher fee), letting you make repeat visits without reapplying each time.

faqs.q: Does my bank statement need to be in GBP?
faqs.a: No — it can stay in NPR, but UKVI expects your application to also state the GBP equivalent using the official exchange rate at the time you apply, so include that conversion alongside your NPR figures.

notes: Fees are reviewed periodically by the Home Office — always check the official fee calculator before applying rather than relying on a remembered figure. A standing police clearance certificate is not part of the standard Standard Visitor visa checklist; the application form itself asks about any criminal history, and further documents are only requested case-by-case. If you're using property as part of your ties-to-Nepal evidence, a lalpurja (land ownership certificate) with an English translation is the typical document Nepali applicants submit.
sourceNotes: Official UK Home Office visa fee calculator (visa-fees.homeoffice.gov.uk) for Nepal, and gov.uk/standard-visitor.

summary: Short-stay Schengen visa — EUR 80 standard fee (EU-wide), apply through the consulate of your main destination country via VFS Global Kathmandu.
overview: A single Schengen visa lets you travel across all 29 Schengen countries on one application. The application fee (EUR 80 for adults, EUR 40 for children 6-12) is set at EU level and is the same regardless of which Schengen country you apply through. The key rule to understand: you apply through the consulate of your 'main destination' — the country where you'll spend the most nights, or if that's evenly split, your first point of entry. Most Nepal-based applicants go through VFS Global Kathmandu, which represents several Schengen countries' consulates (exact list changes periodically, so confirm the current one for your specific destination country before applying).

steps.title: Identify your main destination country
steps.description: This determines which country's consulate handles your application — it isn't a free choice. If you're visiting several Schengen countries, it's the one where you'll spend the most nights.

steps.title: Check which visa centre handles that country from Nepal
steps.description: Most, but not all, Schengen countries process Nepal applications through VFS Global Kathmandu. A few handle applications differently — check the specific embassy's current arrangement before assuming.

steps.title: Book an appointment and complete the application
steps.description: Submit the Schengen application form, photos, and biometrics (fingerprints are reused if given within the past 5 years for a prior Schengen visa).

steps.title: Pay the fee and wait for a decision
steps.description: Standard processing is up to 15 calendar days, though it can extend to 30-45 days in individual cases.

requiredDocuments: Passport issued within the last 10 years, valid at least 3 months beyond your planned departure from the Schengen area, with at least 2 blank pages
Completed and signed Schengen visa application form
One recent ICAO-compliant passport photo (white background, taken within 6 months)
Copy of your Nepali citizenship certificate/ID and all used passport pages
Confirmed round-trip flight reservation and a day-by-day travel itinerary
Accommodation proof for every night of the trip (hotel booking, rental confirmation, or a signed invitation letter from your host)
Travel/medical insurance valid across the whole Schengen area, covering at least EUR 30,000, including emergency medical treatment and repatriation
Original bank statement covering the last 3-6 months (requirement varies by country — 6 months is the safer default), stamped and signed by the bank on every page
If employed: employer letter confirming your position, salary and approved leave, plus your last 3 months' salary slips
If self-employed: PAN/business registration and 6 months' business bank statements
If retired: pension statements or other proof of income covering the last 3 months
Income tax return (ITR) for the last 1-2 years, requested by some Schengen countries (e.g. Austria asks for 2 years)

Property ownership documents (lalpurja) and property tax clearance, as supporting evidence of ties to Nepal — not mandatory everywhere, but explicitly requested by some missions (e.g. the Czech checklist for Nepal names this directly)
Certified English translation for any submitted document that isn't already in English, French, German or Spanish
processingTime: Up to 15 calendar days standard, but can extend to 30-45 days for individual cases — apply well ahead of travel
fee: EUR 90 for adults, EUR 45 for children aged 6-12 (EU-wide standard Schengen fee, effective since the June 2024 increase). Visa centre service fees are charged separately on top of this.
maxStay: Up to 90 days within any 180-day period across the whole Schengen area

officialLinks.label: EU Schengen Visa Information

faqs.q: Can I choose which Schengen country to apply through?
faqs.a: No — you must apply through your main destination country's consulate. Applying through a different country than your actual main destination can lead to refusal.

faqs.q: Does the fee change depending on which Schengen country I'm visiting?
faqs.a: No — EUR 80 is set at EU level and is the same everywhere, though the visa centre's separate service fee can vary slightly by provider.

notes: None of the current Schengen checklists for Nepal require a police clearance certificate for a short-stay tourist visa — it's not part of the standard document list. Property documents (the lalpurja) are the closest thing Nepal has to the "proof of assets/ties" that several Schengen missions ask for — bring the original plus a certified English translation if you own property, since at least one mission's own checklist names it explicitly. Any document issued in Nepali needs a certified English translation: a licensed Notary Public in Kathmandu can certify that the translation is a true and faithful rendering of the original, which is normally sufficient — full Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation (Department of Consular Services, Tripureshwor) is only needed if the specific mission asks for it on top of notarization.
sourceNotes: EU-wide Schengen fee and processing time are set by the EU Visa Code (well-established, publicly documented figures); Nepal-specific visa centre routing confirmed via the Swedish Embassy Nepal fee page as one example, but this should be checked per destination country since routing arrangements are the least stable part of this entry.

summary: e-Visa via a UAE-based sponsor (airline, hotel, or agent) — Nepalis are not visa-exempt, and can't apply without one.
overview: Nepali citizens need a UAE tourist visa, and unlike some nationalities, it cannot be requested directly from a government portal without a sponsor. Every UAE tourist e-Visa is filed by a UAE-based sponsor — commonly an airline (e.g. Emirates, Etihad, flydubai), a hotel you're booking with, a UAE-based travel agency, or a UAE resident/company. You don't need to fly with the sponsoring airline or stay at the sponsoring hotel — sponsorship and your actual travel plans are separate. The visa itself is issued as an e-Visa by email once approved.

steps.title: Choose a sponsor
steps.description: Options: book with an airline that offers visa sponsorship (many major carriers do), book a hotel that offers visa processing, or use a licensed UAE travel agency. Compare fees — they vary between sponsors.

steps.title: Submit documents to the sponsor
steps.description: Passport copy, a digital photo, and payment. Most sponsors handle this through a simple online form.

steps.title: Wait for approval
steps.description: Typically 3-5 working days for a standard tourist e-Visa.

steps.title: Receive and print your e-Visa
steps.description: You'll get it by email as a PDF — bring a printed or digital copy for check-in and immigration.

requiredDocuments: Valid passport with at least 6 months' validity, first and last page copies
Recent passport-style digital photo
Confirmed return or onward flight ticket
Hotel booking confirmation (sometimes requested, depending on sponsor)
Bank statement (occasionally requested, particularly for business-purpose visas or if your sponsor's agency asks for one)
Invitation letter from a UAE host/corporate event organiser, for business visas
processingTime: Typically 3-5 working days
fee: Commonly cited around AED 395-450 (roughly USD 110-125) for a 30-day single-entry tourist visa via a travel agent sponsor; airline-sponsored visas may price differently. Confirm the exact fee with your chosen sponsor before paying, since this is a market rate set by sponsors, not a fixed government fee.
maxStay: Typically 30 or 90 days depending on which visa product you choose, single or multiple entry

officialLinks.label: UAE Federal Authority (ICP) — general visa information

faqs.q: Do I need to fly with or stay at my sponsor's business?
faqs.a: No — most sponsors only require you to hold the visa they issue; you can typically book your own flights and accommodation separately unless the specific sponsor's terms say otherwise.

faqs.q: Is there a direct government e-visa I can apply for myself, with no sponsor?
faqs.a: No — UAE tourist visas for Nepali citizens are issued through a licensed sponsor (an airline, hotel, or visa agent), not a self-service government portal.

notes: Because this route runs through commercial sponsors (airlines, hotels, or licensed visa agents) rather than a single government application, exact document asks vary by provider — comparing 2-3 licensed sponsors before paying is worth the few minutes it takes. No police clearance certificate or property document is generally required for a standard tourist visit visa; these become relevant mainly for UAE work/residency visas, which are a different category from the short tourist visa covered here.
sourceNotes: UAE visa-sponsorship structure confirmed via UAE ICP and multiple independent travel-visa guides describing the sponsor requirement and typical agent pricing.

summary: e-Visa required in advance — Nepal is NOT on Thailand's visa-on-arrival list, despite what many older articles claim.
overview: Nepali passport holders need a Thai tourist e-Visa applied for online before travel — Nepal has never been on Thailand's visa-on-arrival country list (that list covers about 30 specific countries, mostly not including South Asia). Thailand also overhauled its broader visa-exemption system on 15 September 2026, tightening rules generally, so it's worth double-checking current requirements close to your travel date since this is a recently and actively changing area of policy.

steps.title: Apply on the official e-Visa portal
steps.description: Submit your application at thaievisa.go.th — the official Royal Thai Government portal. Avoid third-party sites that charge extra service fees for the same process.

steps.title: Upload required documents
steps.description: Passport photo page, a recent passport-style photo, proof of accommodation, and a return/onward flight ticket.

steps.title: Pay the e-Visa fee online
steps.description: Paid directly through the official portal.

steps.title: Complete the Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC)
steps.description: Required separately, before arrival, regardless of visa type — this is a newer requirement and easy to overlook.

Recent passport-style photo
Confirmed return or onward flight ticket
Proof of accommodation in Thailand for the full stay
Detailed day-by-day travel itinerary
Updated 6-month bank statement showing a minimum balance of THB 20,000 (about NPR 80,000) per person, or THB 40,000 (about NPR 160,000) for a family application
Thailand Digital Arrival Card (completed separately before arrival)

fee: Set on the official e-Visa portal — check thaievisa.go.th directly for the current amount rather than relying on third-party estimates, which vary widely.
maxStay: Typically up to 60 days on the standard tourist (TR) e-Visa, single entry, though this should be confirmed at application time given the recent policy overhaul.

faqs.q: Can I just get a visa on arrival like some travelers from other countries?
faqs.a: No — Nepal has never been on Thailand's visa-on-arrival eligible list. This is a common misconception from outdated blog posts. Nepali travelers must arrange a visa before departure.

notes: This THB 20,000/40,000 minimum-balance figure comes from the Royal Thai Embassy in Kathmandu's own published requirements for its Tourist Visa 'TR' route; if you apply via Thailand's eVisa system instead, use the same figures as a safe planning minimum since the underlying financial-proof expectation is the same. No property document or police clearance certificate is required for the tourist route.

summary: e-Visa via the official government portal — USD 25 single-entry / USD 50 multiple-entry, valid up to 90 days.
overview: Nepali citizens can apply for a Vietnam e-Visa entirely online through the official government portal, with no embassy visit needed. Vietnam opened e-Visa eligibility to essentially all nationalities in 2023, and it now offers both single-entry and multiple-entry options valid up to 90 days. Apply only on the official government site — many commercial 'visa service' sites charge large markups for the same process.

steps.title: Upload documents and pay the fee
steps.description: Upload a photo of your passport's personal details page and a portrait photo, then pay the government fee online (charged in VND, equivalent to about USD 25 or USD 50).

steps.title: Wait for approval
steps.description: Approval typically takes a few business days; check status using your registration code on the official portal.

steps.title: Print your e-Visa
steps.description: Download and print the approved e-Visa to present on arrival — immigration checks the printed or digital copy at the border.

Digital photo of your passport's personal details page
Passport-style digital portrait photo
Active email address for confirmation and to download your approved eVisa
processingTime: Typically a few business days on the official portal
fee: USD 25 (single-entry, 30 days) or USD 50 (multiple-entry, up to 90 days), paid in VND-equivalent on the official portal. Third-party 'visa service' sites often charge USD 55-160+ for the same e-Visa — avoid these unless you specifically want paid expediting help.
maxStay: Up to 90 days depending on the e-Visa type chosen (30-day and 90-day options both exist)

faqs.a: No — the official government portal (evisa.gov.vn) handles the same application directly for the government fee only. Paid services just add a markup for filling out the same form on your behalf.

notes: Vietnam's tourist eVisa is one of the simplest in this list for Nepali applicants — no bank statement, property document, or police clearance certificate is required. Return or onward travel ticket

summary: Sticker visa via VFS Global Kathmandu — NPR 2,780 visa fee + NPR 2,430 service fee, about 6 working days.

steps.title: Submit at VFS Global Kathmandu
steps.description: Submit your application and biometrics (if applicable) at the Japan Visa Application Centre in Kathmandu.

steps.title: Pay the visa fee and service fee
steps.description: Visa fee (NPR 2,780) and VFS service fee (NPR 2,430, tax-inclusive) are paid together at submission.

steps.title: Wait for a decision

Valid passport with at least one blank page

summary: Sticker visa via the Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Kathmandu — required for all Nepali tourists (no visa-on-arrival or K-ETA option). Current single-entry tourist fee is NPR 5,400.
overview: South Korea requires Nepali tourists to obtain a sticker (C-3 short-term) visa in person from the Korean Embassy in Kathmandu before travel — there is no visa-on-arrival, and Nepal is not on Korea's K-ETA eligibility list. The embassy revises its fee schedule periodically via its own notices, so it's worth a quick check before you apply.

steps.title: Gather required documents
steps.description: Passport, photo, travel itinerary, accommodation proof, and bank statements showing sufficient funds.

steps.title: Book an appointment and submit your application
steps.description: Book a submission appointment online in advance with the Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Kathmandu — submission days are limited (typically Monday and Wednesday mornings) — then submit your application in person at that slot (or through an authorized visa agency, if the embassy directs applicants there for your visa type).

steps.title: Pay the visa fee
steps.description: Fee changed as of 1 January 2026 — verify the current amount with the embassy or its official notice board before applying.

steps.title: Wait for a decision

Completed visa application form with a glued (not stapled) photo
Cover letter describing your purpose of visit, itinerary and sponsorship (if any)
Round-trip flight booking with a valid reservation reference
Hotel confirmation showing the full address and contact details
Personal bank statement covering the last 6 months, from an A-class bank
Employment certificate from your employer or educational institution
PAN and business registration (original and copy), if self-employed
Balance certificate demonstrating financial stability
TB (tuberculosis) medical report from a designated hospital
Asset evaluation certificate, certified by a chartered accountant

nearestEmbassy.note: Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Nepal handles visa issuance directly — appointments must be booked online in advance (submission days are limited, typically Monday and Wednesday mornings).

faqs.q: Can I use K-ETA instead of a visa, like some other nationalities?
faqs.a: No — Nepal is not on Korea's K-ETA eligibility list, so a full sticker visa from the Embassy is required for every Nepali tourist.

faqs.q: What is the 'asset evaluation certificate' and do I really need one?
faqs.a: It's a certified valuation of your property or other assets, prepared by a chartered accountant — Korea's tourist visa checklist for Nepali applicants lists it alongside your bank statement as financial proof.
